newsitem.title: UK: Copper backtracks in late LME, still ends higher.
newsitem.headline: Copper backtracks in late LME, still ends higher.

text.p: Copper prices ended firmer but below early peaks during nervous Wednesday afternoon trading on the London Metal Exchange where traders said that a volatile market was trying tried to gauge direction.
Prices at one stage ran up to $2,083, highest for more than two months, on spread tightness, speculative buying and expectations of further inventory falls.
But there was some stiff resistance and liquidation above $2,075 with the market also unsettled by a WBMS report that there may be substantial non-LME stocks in the Netherlands.
Traders said the physical market is tight, noting a shortage of scrap and off-grade, and with LME stocks seen falling by another "five-figure" amount on Friday declines were cushioned.
At the end of the kerb three months was last at $2,060, a $15 gain from Tuesday, with traders eying another test of $2,070/75 in the short-term.
The cash/threes backardation also remained solid at $75/80, and is seen heading towards $100 as November/December tightens and, further out, late January 1997 dates become a focus of attention.
Aluminium struggled to maintain levels above $1,450, against a background of slow physical demand, and drifted back to end the kerb at $1,442.50, down $12 from yesterday.
Nickel prices were partially supported by news that Russia's Norilsk may have some assets seized because of tax arrears, but the market was unable to make any real headway.
Values slid lower during the afternoon kerb, relinquishing the $7,200 level, and closed at $7,170, a $60 loss from Tuesday.
There was little excitement in the lead market, with prices meandering around the $740 level for most of the day until a late kerb decline. Final trade was at $738, against a previous $737.
Zinc business was equally unexciting, with a midsession flip up towards $1,070 not sustained, and last trade was at $1,063, down $1.
Tin attempted to clear the $6,000 level on several occasions, but faltered each time and sagged back to close the kerb at $5,990, still up $10 from Tuesday.
The alloy market was subdued and finished at $1,300/02 a tonne, versus the overnight close of $1,305/1,308.
